CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction consultation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. She has been considering this procedure for approximately six to seven years. She reports experiencing back pain and neck pain since high school, which she attributes in part to her breast size. She describes pain in the upper back and neck that builds up, particularly when working at a desk all day. She has been seeing a chiropractor for a few years. She reports bra strap indentations on her shoulders. She denies rashes underneath the breasts but notes they are always sweaty. She reports sometimes experiencing numbness or tingling in the hands and some nipple pain. She feels her activities are limited because of breast size, particularly with working out, jumping, and running, which cause pain. She wears a 34E sports bra most often due to comfort and cost. She has not had any children but may plan to have children in the future. She has not previously consulted with anyone about breast reduction. Regarding breast cancer screening, her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40, and she has been recommended to start mammograms at age 30 but has not yet started as she is currently 25 years old.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Sometimes experiences numbness or tingling in the hands. Sometimes experiences nipple pain. Denies rashes underneath breasts. Breasts are always sweaty.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Has been seeing a chiropractor for a few years for back pain.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol (migraine medication).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently studying psychology. Drinks wine occasionally. Denies tobacco and drug use. Has lost approximately 10 pounds over the past few months and desires to lose approximately 20 more pounds. Will be changing insurance providers in July when her husband starts a new job; currently has Blue Cross Blue Shield.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy is palpable. One breast is noted to be slightly lower than the other.

RESULTS
Body surface area is 2.65. Minimum required resection based on Schnur scale is 1,792 grams. Patient measurements obtained.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. Patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Surgery typically takes about three hours and involves making an incision around the nipple, straight down and underneath (anchor-shaped incision), through which tissue is removed and breast is lifted with nipple elevation. Expected post-operative size approximately small C cup. Patient will have drains (one in each side) for approximately one week. Clear plastic tape will be placed over incisions to help with scars. One night hospital stay recommended for pain control and monitoring for nausea. Activity restrictions for approximately six weeks post-operatively, no heavy lifting, no driving for two to three weeks. Approximately 30% of patients cannot breastfeed after the procedure. Breast sensation typically remains intact unless massive reduction. Bruising is normal post-operatively. Scars typically appear red initially and take about one year to mature. Potential for nipple graft given breast size and measurements. Patient is ready to proceed once insurance is switched over in July. Plan to obtain photos today. Documentation of symptoms provided to patient. Once new insurance information is obtained by patient, office will submit for insurance approval. Upon approval, office will coordinate surgery date and schedule pre-operative visit to review instructions and answer final questions.
